text:
Sophie (AE): Quick sync — customer wants a fully isolated POC (no outbound internet, air-gapped). They asked what we deliver for install artifacts and how upgrades work. timeline: want POC next month.
Marco (SE): They do on-prem k8s 1.25. Curious if they can use an operator or do we need a full tarball install?
Connor (Packaging): We can do both. Operator/helm is easiest if they have an internal registry. For fully disconnected sites we provide a signed offline bundle (tar.gz) + SBOM + delta patch bundles for upgrades.
Leah (SecOps): Security checklist items from their team: SBOM, image signing verification, reproducible checksums, offline license activation, and a way to attest bundles in their supply chain scanner. Also need to know how long upgrade windows typically take.
Sophie (AE): Also pricing question — they asked if POC license covers upgrades/patches during trial.
Marco (SE): For install flow options: 1) internal registry flow: we publish images -> customer pulls into their registry (we provide image list and signed digests). 2) bundle flow: customer scp's tarball to airgap node and runs an install script. 3) ephemeral proxy: short-lived bastion to pull images once. Which do we support today?
Connor (Packaging): All three. For bundle flow we include: artifacts/, sbom.json, checksums.txt.asc, install.sh, and a metadata manifest. We sign the bundle with cosign + our key and provide verification instructions. Example verify snippet we give customers:

```bash
# verify signature (cosign public key provided in secure channel)
cosign verify-blob --key redwood_pub.key checksums.txt.asc
sha256sum -c checksums.txt
```

Connor (Packaging): Delta upgrades: we ship incremental patch archives (layer diffs) that apply on top of existing bundle. That reduces transfer size in air-gapped environments. Upgrade tool validates signature and SBOM before applying.
Leah (SecOps): Need to confirm threat model: who can generate signed bundles? We require enterprise SSO-approved engineers and HSM-backed signing for GA. For POC we can use a temporary key, but customer wants audit logs + proof of key custody.
Sophie (AE): Timeline constraint — customer says procurement will only sign if rollback + patch cadence is clear. They want documented rollback steps for each minor upgrade.
Marco (SE): Rollback is supported for patches that touch non-destructive migrations. We include a dry-run flag in the upgrade tool and backup snapshots of PVs where applicable. Example command:

```bash
./redwood-upgrade --apply patch-2026-11 --dry-run --backup /mnt/backups && ./redwood-upgrade --apply patch-2026-11
```

Connor (Packaging): For the air-gapped POC we need these from the customer: 1) NAT-able bastion host (optional), 2) list of allowed internal registry URLs, 3) k8s kubeconfig with cluster-admin for install, 4) contact for on-call during install.
Leah (SecOps): We'll provide a template SBOM and an example signing key rotation doc. For the audit piece, deploy-bot will emit install/startup events to the customer log collector via file-based forwarder (no outbound).
Sophie (AE): Pricing: can we offer a 30-day POC license that includes cold-path OS patching and two upgrade patches? Customer asked about 'free upgrades during trial'.
Connor (Packaging): We usually include onboarding + one patch during trial. Additional patches or extended delta support can be scoped into SOW.
Leah (SecOps): Also note that some customers demand vulnerability scanning of images before acceptance. We can provide SBOM and a scan report (Snyk/Clair) as part of the bundle.
Marco (SE): Any blockers from engineering to produce a signed bundle + delta workflow in 3 weeks?
Connor (Packaging): We can generate a POC bundle next week if they provide image whitelist. Delta tooling is already in infra but I'll need to produce the specific patch archive and a verification checklist.
Sophie (AE): Action items: @Marco confirm installer variant with customer; @Connor prepare a sample signed bundle + verification steps; @Leah prepare SBOM + signing key custody note and a short rollback doc. I'll ask procurement if 30-day POC + one patch is acceptable.
Leah (SecOps): +1 on items. Also I'll add a short paragraph for their security team about HSM signing vs temp keys for POC.
deploy-bot: upload completed: redwood-offline-bundle-v0.1.tar.gz -> staged (checksum: sha256:abc123...)
